title: The Flats
status: prose treatment complete; graphic script draft complete
summary: Introduce Harbor Phase as a functioning, automated, emotionally flattening city. Establish the six leads as materially safe but structurally unnecessary. A rumored extreme low-tide Reach window pulls the old group back together. They gather at the floodwall, cross the exposed flats through mud and fog, and see the Reach emerge as an interrupted offshore future.
opening_image: Rain over Harbor Phase; automated systems absorbing inconvenience before people feel it.
ending_image: The group small on exposed seabed, Harbor Phase dim behind them, the Reach huge and unfinished ahead through fog.

key_dialogue.text: They built farther out than maps say.

title: The Dead Mall
status: prose treatment complete; graphic script draft complete
summary: The group enters the Near Reach, finds informal runner markings, and discovers Fashion Harbor Center. The flooded mall becomes the first place where the Reach feels socially occupied: upper floors, work lights, noodles, cracked maps, jokes, and temporary trust. The chapter shifts from awe to belonging, then lets the building groan and the tide remind them they cannot stay. They exit toward the Glass Rail.
opening_image: The group advances into outer structures while Ryan reads water channels instead of skyline scale.
ending_image: A broken elevated walkway from the dead mall toward the Glass Rail; the mall alive behind them, black water returning below.

key_dialogue.text: Everything here was built for people exactly like us.
The Reach did not feel empty anymore. That was the dangerous part.

title: No Signal
status: prose treatment complete; graphic script draft complete
summary: Repeat crossings make impossibility familiar. Tide culture develops route names, wall marks, oral stories, and temporary reputation. Harbor Market Roof becomes a social high where no signal forces presence. Matt becomes useful, Chris starts shaping stories, Justin tests attention, Nicole studies planned connections, Kevin is right softly, and Ryan watches the tide instead of the crowd. The chapter ends with Ryan warning Matt that the Reach is not land; it is tide being temporarily absent.
opening_image: Packed bags and repeated crossing rituals begin replacing inland calendars.
ending_image: The group leaves Harbor Market Roof into fog; the first time leaving felt like survival, this time it feels like being sent home.

key_dialogue.text: It mattered to whoever drew it.
For a while, everyone had a use.

title: Between Runs
status: prose treatment complete; graphic script pending
summary: The Reach becomes dependency. Tide windows replace normal calendars, inland relationships drift, Nicole builds a map room, Justin becomes locally known for dangerous climbs, Chris mythologizes risk, Matt becomes territorial, and commercialization contaminates the social space. The group cracks. Ryan pulls away after seeing everyone treat the Reach as identity instead of water.
opening_image: Packed gear by apartment doors; tide windows replacing ordinary obligations.
ending_image: Ryan alone near the floodwall, seeing the group's safety structure shift while the others think they are improving.

key_dialogue.text: It is real. That’s why it’s going to hurt somebody.
